question: According to the review on water quality as a barrier to photocatalytic green hydrogen, what share of the world's hydrogen is still produced from fossil fuels, and in what year did Fujishima and Honda report photoelectrochemical water splitting?
rendered:
The document "Water quality as an economic barrier to photocatalytic green hydrogen production" contains the answer.

According to the text on page 1, nearly 95% of the world's hydrogen is still produced from fossil fuels through processes such as steam methane reforming and coal gasification.

According to the text on page 3, Fujishima and Honda reported photoelectrochemical water splitting in 1972.
